title: 读后续写　写作第二节 · 练习
goal: 在 25 分钟内接着原文写出两段约 150 词、情节连贯的故事。

points.label: 使情节符合原文线索与因果关系
用具体动作展现情节发展
保持叙事人称与时态一致

sources.title: 2024 年高考综合改革适应性测试 英语（新课标卷）试卷（教育部教育考试院）
sources.used: 写作第二节的任务形式、两段约 150 词和满分 25 分

cards.title: 评分标准：每一档长什么样
cards.note: 读后续写满分 25 分，这里按 5 分一段分为五档，与批改的 5—1 分对应。官方各档描述尚未确认，各档说法依据本练习的三项能力编写。

levels.name: 21—25 分
levels.summary: 情节与原文和两个段首句衔接自然，发展合理、结局完整；用动作、对话和心理细节呈现变化；人称时态一致，语言准确丰富。
signs: 第一段的结尾自然引出第二段的段首句。
情节由原文的线索和人物目标推动，没有突然的转折。
几乎没有语言错误，句式有变化。

levels.name: 16—20 分
levels.summary: 情节与原文和段首句衔接较好，内容较完整；有一定细节；语言较准确，少量错误不影响理解。
signs: 情节合理，个别环节交代得简单。
有具体动作或对话，但多处仍是概括叙述。

levels.name: 11—15 分
levels.summary: 情节基本合理，但与原文线索或第二段段首句衔接不够；细节较少；语言错误较多，部分影响理解。
signs: 用了原文的部分线索，第一段的结果与第二段段首句有脱节。
以「他很高兴」「问题解决了」这类概括为主。
时态混用或句子结构错误看得出来。

levels.name: 6—10 分
levels.summary: 情节与原文有明显脱节或矛盾；几乎没有细节；人称时态混乱，错误多。
signs: 改变了原文已有的事实，或另起一个故事。
只交代结果，看不到人物怎样做到。

levels.name: 1—5 分
levels.summary: 只写出零星相关内容；语言错误严重且频繁，难以理解。
signs: 可辨认的相关情节很少。
大部分句子无法读懂，或主要照抄原文。

levels.name: 0 分
levels.summary: 未作答，或内容与原文无关。
signs: 空白、只抄原文或写的不是英语。

takeaways.d: 第二段的段首句规定了第一段结束时必须发生的事。先想清楚这一步，再安排第一段的过程。
两档的情节都说得通。差别在于细节：4 档能看到人物的具体动作和对话，3 档多是概括的结果。
原文用一般过去时叙述，续写也用一般过去时；回指更早的事用过去完成时。

cards.title: 批改单：每次都按这个格式给

format.d: 逐条判：做到了、做了但太薄、没做。每条引续写里的一句原话作依据。
0—5 中选一档，加一句理由，用评分标准里的说法。
最多五处，按对理解的影响从大到小排，时态和动词形式排在最前。每处给原句、改后的句子和一句规则。
挑一到两句重写成高一档的写法：把概括的结果改成具体的动作或对话。满档的续写不改写。

cards.rules: 批改单里不写鼓励的话，也不评价写作者。0—5 分依次对应评分标准的六档，是课程的估计，不是高考实际得分。

example.about: 以「阅读角的纸灯笼」一题中的一篇续写为例。

coverage.bullet: Develop the plot using the clues and causes in the story.
coverage.quote: Maya decided to use the ribbon to hang the lanterns on the hooks.
coverage.note: 用上了原文的丝带和挂钩两条线索。

coverage.bullet: Show the development through specific actions.
coverage.quote: They worked very hard and finished it quickly.
coverage.note: 只说结果，看不到谁做了什么。

coverage.bullet: Keep the narrative person and tense consistent.
coverage.quote: Ben holds the chair and Maya climbs up.
coverage.note: 原文用一般过去时，这里改成了一般现在时。

example.reason: 情节基本合理，用了原文线索；细节较少，以概括叙述为主；时态混用看得出来。

fixes.from: Ben holds the chair and Maya climbs up.
fixes.to: Ben held the chair and Maya climbed up.
fixes.rule: 叙事保持一般过去时，与原文一致。
主语 visitors 是复数，谓语用 were。

upgrade.from: They worked very hard and finished it quickly.
upgrade.to: The boy passed her the lanterns one by one, and Ben carried the other end of the ribbon across to the second hook.
upgrade.why: 把概括的结果改成三个人各自的动作，情节发展看得见。

tasks.setting:
On the morning of the school fair, Maya carried a cardboard box into the hall. It held the paper lanterns her class had made for the reading corner. Each lantern had a small paper label with the title of a book written on it. Visitors could choose a label, find the book on the shelf and leave a short recommendation for the next reader.

Maya and her friend Ben had planned the corner for weeks. Ben had brought a wooden stand from home, and Maya had promised to hang the lanterns before the doors opened. They wanted the youngest visitors to find the books without having to ask for help.

As Maya placed the box on a table, she heard a soft crack. One side of the stand had come loose. Ben examined it and found that a small wooden peg had fallen out. They searched the floor, but the hall was already crowded with tables, bags and boxes. The peg was nowhere in sight.

There were only twenty minutes left. Maya suggested putting the lanterns directly on the shelf, but Ben shook his head. The shelf was too low, and the labels would be hidden behind the books. He hurried off to ask a teacher for tools, while Maya tried to keep the lanterns from rolling off the table.

Then a younger student stopped beside her. He had been helping to arrange the chairs, and he held a handful of coloured ribbon left over from another display. Maya remembered seeing two hooks above the reading corner. She looked at the ribbon, then at the lanterns. The student noticed her expression and asked what was wrong. Before she could answer, Ben returned without the tools: the teacher had lent them to another group. The doors would open in ten minutes, and the stand still leaned against the wall.

Paragraph 1: Maya pointed to the hooks above the reading corner.
Paragraph 2: When the doors opened, the first visitors came towards the corner.
tasks.lead: Continue the story in two paragraphs of about 150 words in total. Begin each paragraph with its given sentence.
bullets: Develop the plot using the clues and causes in the story.
Show the development through specific actions.
Keep the narrative person and tense consistent.
must: 使情节符合原文线索与因果关系
用具体动作展现情节发展
保持叙事人称与时态一致
tasks.model:
Maya pointed to the hooks above the reading corner. "We can hang the lanterns from there with this ribbon," she said. The younger student's eyes lit up, and he handed her the ribbon at once. Ben fetched a chair and held it steady while Maya climbed up. She tied one end of the ribbon to the first hook, and the boy passed her the lanterns one by one. Ben slid each lantern onto the ribbon and carried the other end across to the second hook. Just as Maya tied the last knot, a teacher announced that the doors were about to open.

When the doors opened, the first visitors came towards the corner. A little girl stopped under a red lantern, read its label aloud and ran to the shelf to find the book. Maya smiled at Ben and the younger student. Even without the stand, the youngest visitors could find their books without asking for help.

tasks.setting:
Every Sunday, Grandpa Joe walked to the pond in the park to feed the ducks. This spring, however, his knee had become painful, and the walk took him much longer than before. His granddaughter Ella, who was twelve, decided to go with him.

One Sunday in April, they found the gate to the pond path locked. A sign said that the path was being repaired and that visitors should use the north entrance. Ella checked the map on the sign. The north entrance was on the other side of the park, almost a kilometre away. Grandpa Joe looked at the long road and sighed. "Maybe the ducks will have to wait until next week," he said, trying to smile.

Ella did not want to give up so easily. She remembered that her school had borrowed a wheelchair from the park office for a sports day last year. The office was only a short walk away, beside the café. But Grandpa Joe hated asking for help. He had always been the one who helped others, fixing the neighbours' fences and carrying their shopping.

"Grandpa, wait here on the bench for a moment," Ella said. Before he could reply, she ran towards the café, holding the bag of bread for the ducks so tightly that it crackled.

At the office, a young woman in a green uniform listened to her. She explained that a wheelchair was available, but an adult had to sign for it in person. Ella's heart sank. Her mother was at work, and she was not sure that Grandpa Joe would agree to sit in a wheelchair at all. She looked out of the window at the bench in the distance, where her grandfather sat alone with his walking stick.

Paragraph 1: Ella hurried back to the bench and told Grandpa Joe about the wheelchair.
Paragraph 2: Twenty minutes later, they reached the north side of the pond.

tasks.model:
Ella hurried back to the bench and told Grandpa Joe about the wheelchair. He shook his head at once. "I'm not that old," he said. Ella sat down beside him and opened the bag of bread. "You always carry Mrs Brown's shopping for her," she said softly. "Today, let me help you. The ducks are waiting." Grandpa Joe looked at the bread, then at her hopeful face. At last he laughed, picked up his walking stick and walked slowly with her to the office, where he signed the form himself.

Twenty minutes later, they reached the north side of the pond. As soon as Ella pushed the wheelchair to the water's edge, the ducks swam towards them, quacking loudly. Grandpa Joe threw the first piece of bread and watched them race for it. "You know," he said, "accepting help isn't so hard after all." Ella grinned and handed him another piece.
